title: optimize: dynamic batching by sequence length with bucketing and padding minimization
author: Aisha Rahman
description:
Motivation: mixed-length request workloads cause significant padding waste when naively batching by arrival time. This PR implements a sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization layer in the continuous batcher, combines it with seqlen-aware scheduling heuristics, and adds safety integrations with the KV cache to avoid cache churn during re-bucketing. The goal is to reduce wasted tokens, improve throughput for heterogeneous workloads, and lower tail latency for short requests.

What this change does: adds a new SeqlenBucketScheduler that groups inflight requests into buckets by effective context length (request_length + expected_generation_length) and only pads within each bucket to the bucket max, rather than the global max. The batcher uses an adaptive bucketing heuristic derived from historic seqlen histograms and a per-GPU memory budget to choose bucket boundaries at runtime. A short list of tunables were added: seqlen_bucketing_enabled (bool), max_bucket_pad_ratio (float), min_bucket_fill (int), bucket_merge_threshold (float), and max_batch_tokens (int).

KV cache & scheduling: To avoid evicting KV caches when resizing internal execution buffers, the scheduler signals the KVCacheManager before committing a bucketed batch. If a planned bucket would cause a cache invalidation (observed in some 8-bit quantization combos), the bucket is either split or delayed. We also added heuristics to prefer seating short requests into short-request buckets to reduce tail latency. A fairness policy ensures long requests are not starved by setting a maximum delay window and a fallback to size-based batching.

Kernels & performance: The runtime kernel selection path was extended to prefer smaller-sequence kernels when the bucket max is significantly smaller than the previous average; this yields better memory/locality behavior for short-request heavy buckets. We also added a tiny fast-path that collapses identical-seqlen requests into a single multi-copy dispatch to reduce kernel launch overhead.

Benchmarks & results: see bench/bench_dybatching_seqlen.py for harness. On our mixed-AI production trace (50% short <64 tokens, 30% medium 64-512, 20% long >512):
- Throughput improved ~12-18% tokens/sec depending on GPU type (A100 p4d -> 18%, V100-like config -> 12%).
- Average per-request token padding reduced by ~42% (measured padding tokens / total tokens).
- 95th-percentile latency for short requests improved 20-35% depending on load.
- Cost model simulation shows ~10-22% per-token compute cost reduction for the trace.

Safety, tests & CI: unit tests for bucketing logic and padding minimizer added. End-to-end bench tests included; CI runs against a fast synthetic trace and a representative perf runner in nightly. All checks pass in this PR.

Compatibility & rollout: feature gated behind seqlen_bucketing_enabled (false by default). We added a metric seqlen_bucketing.active_buckets and seqlen_bucketing.pad_savings to the observability plane and a canary rollout plan in the console docs. The default heuristics are tuned for A100-like GPUs and conservative memory budgets to avoid regressions on small-memory devices.

Files changed: small, focused runtime changes plus tests and docs. See changelog entry.

Notes: this is iteration v2 of the seqlen bucketing work (previous iterations in the repo); this PR focuses on making the algorithm robust across quantization & KV cache boundaries and adding the scheduler fallbacks to ensure production stability.

Integrate padding minimizer into continuous batcher
KV cache handshake for bucket commits and safety checks
Add kernel fast-path for identical seqlen multi-dispatch
Add unit tests, bench harness, and docs
Fix kv cache invalidation edge case and race in scheduler

release_notes: Improved dynamic batching: added adaptive sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization for heterogeneous workloads. Expected throughput gains on mixed-length traces and reduced padding waste. Feature is off by default and gated by seqlen_bucketing_enabled.
